q: In physics, work is defined as the _____ product of the force applied and the displacement.
e: Work is the scalar product of force and displacement, W = Fs cos θ. In physics, work is defined as the scalar product of the force applied and the displacement. Do not trade scalar for vector or tensor.

q: The rate of doing work is defined as _____.
e: Power is work per unit time. In SI that unit is the watt: 1 W = 1 J s⁻¹. The rate of doing work is defined as power. Energy or efficiency is not this quantity.

q: The unit for power in SI units is the _____.
e: SI power is the watt. Erg per second is CGS. Horsepower is the British engineering unit. The unit for power in SI units is the watt.

q: If the work done is 1 joule in 1 second, the power is _____.
e: One joule in one second is one watt. If the work done is 1 joule in 1 second, the power is 1 watt. 10 watts or 0.1 watt is not this quantity.

q: In the CGS system, the unit of power is _____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. In the CGS system, the unit of power is erg s^-1. Do not trade erg s^-1 for watt or horse power.

q: In the British engineering system, the unit of power is _____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. In the British engineering system, the unit of power is horse power. Foot-pound per second or kilowatt is not this quantity.

q: 1 horse power is equal to _____ W.
e: Horsepower is the British engineering unit of power. 1 horse power is equal to 746 W. 550 or 1000 is not this quantity.

q: 1 horse power is equal to _____ ft-lb s$^{-1}$.
e: Horsepower is the British engineering unit of power. 1 horse power is equal to 550 ft-lb s^-1. Do not trade 550 for 746 or 1000.

q: For uniform motion, power is equal to the product of force and _____.
e: At constant speed, power is force times velocity, P = Fv. For uniform motion, power is equal to the product of force and velocity. Displacement or time is not this quantity.

q: The formula for power in terms of force and average velocity is _____.
e: Average velocity is displacement over the time interval, Δr/Δt. The formula for power in terms of force and average velocity is P = Fv. P = Fs or P = F/t is a different relation from P = Fv.

q: 1 W is equal to _____ erg s$^{-1}$.
e: CGS power is the erg per second. 1 W is equal to 10^7 erg s^-1. 10^5 or 10^9 is not this quantity.

q: The unit of power which is larger than watt and equals $10^6$ W is the _____.
e: 1 kW = 10³ W and 1 MW = 10⁶ W. The unit of power which is larger than watt and equals 10^6 W is the megawatt. Gigawatt or kilowatt is not this quantity.

q: A simple machine is a mechanical device that amplifies the magnitude of a force and changes its _____.
e: A simple machine is a mechanical device that amplifies the magnitude of a force and changes its position. Mass or energy is not this quantity.

q: The six simple machines are lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, screw and _____.
e: The six simple machines are lever, wheel and axle, pulley, inclined plane, screw and wedge. Gear or spring is not this quantity.

q: The ratio of load to effort is defined as the _____ of the machine.
e: The ratio of load to effort is defined as the mechanical advantage of the machine. Efficiency or velocity ratio is not this quantity.

q: The formula for mechanical advantage is _____.
e: The formula for mechanical advantage is MA = L / E. MA = E / L or MA = L × E is a different relation from MA = L / E. Ma = l / e is what this sentence is naming. Stay with the quantity named in this sentence.

q: The ratio of the distance moved by the effort to that of the load in the same time is called the _____ of the machine.
e: The ratio of the distance moved by the effort to that of the load in the same time is called the velocity ratio of the machine. Do not trade velocity ratio for mechanical advantage or efficiency.

q: The formula for velocity ratio is _____.
e: The formula for velocity ratio is VR = Seffort / Sload. VR = Sload / Seffort or VR = E / L is a different relation from VR = Seffort / Sload.

q: The ratio of output work to input work is defined as the _____ of the machine.
e: Work is the scalar product of force and displacement, W = Fs cos θ. The ratio of output work to input work is defined as the efficiency of the machine. Do not trade efficiency for mechanical advantage or velocity ratio.

q: Efficiency is generally expressed in the _____ form.
e: Efficiency is generally expressed in the percentage form. Fraction or decimal is not this quantity.

q: The relationship between efficiency, mechanical advantage, and velocity ratio is efficiency = _____.
e: The relationship between efficiency, mechanical advantage, and velocity ratio is efficiency = (MA / VR) × 100%. (VR / MA) × 100% or (MA × VR) × 100% is a different relation from (MA / VR) × 100%.

q: In practice, the efficiency of a machine must always be _____ 100%.
e: In practice, the efficiency of a machine must always be less than 100%. Equal to or greater than is not this quantity.

q: Input work always exceeds output work because some effort is spent in overcoming _____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Input work always exceeds output work because some effort is spent in overcoming friction. Gravity or inertia is not this quantity.

q: Work obtained from a machine when lifting a load is called the _____ work.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. Work obtained from a machine when lifting a load is called the output work. Input or total is not this quantity.

q: Ability to retain the original form when the applied force is removed is called _____.
e: Ability to retain the original form when the applied force is removed is called elasticity. Plasticity or rigidity is not this quantity.

q: _____ is a limit, beyond which if an elastic object is stretched, it will not return to its original form.
e: Elastic limit is a limit, beyond which if an elastic object is stretched, it will not return to its original form. Yield point or breaking point is not this quantity.

q: Hooke's law states that as long as the elastic limit of a body is not exceeded, the _____ produced is proportional to stress causing it.
e: Hooke's law states that as long as the elastic limit of a body is not exceeded, the strain produced is proportional to stress causing it. Stress or force is not this quantity.

q: According to Hooke's law, the applied force is proportional to the _____.
e: According to Hooke's law, the applied force is proportional to the elongation. Do not trade elongation for mass or velocity.

q: The mathematical expression for Hooke's law is _____.
e: The mathematical expression for Hooke's law is F = kx. F = k/x or F = x/k is a different relation from F = kx.

q: In the formula $F = kx$, the constant $k$ is called the _____.
e: In the formula F = kx, the constant k is called the spring constant. Force constant or elastic constant is not this quantity.

q: The unit of spring constant $k$ is _____.
e: The unit of spring constant k is N m^-1. N m or kg m^-1 is not this quantity.

q: The elastic potential energy stored by a stretched spring is given by the formula _____.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The elastic potential energy stored by a stretched spring is given by the formula PE = (1)/(2) k x². PE = kx² or PE = (1)/(2) k x is a different relation from PE = (1)/(2) k x².

q: The work done in stretching a spring is stored as the _____ energy of the spring.
e: Work is F · s. Power is work per second, in watts. The work done in stretching a spring is stored as the potential energy of the spring. Do not trade potential for kinetic or thermal.

q: The amount of elongation is also called _____.
e: The amount of elongation is also called compression. Extension or tension is not this quantity.

q: Energy sources can be classified as two major sources: conventional sources and _____ sources.
e: Energy sources can be classified as two major sources: conventional sources and non-conventional sources. Alternative or secondary is not this quantity.

q: Conventional energy sources are _____ energy sources.
e: Conventional energy sources are non-renewable energy sources. Renewable or sustainable is not this quantity.

q: Non-conventional energy sources are _____ energy sources.
e: Non-conventional energy sources are renewable energy sources. Do not trade renewable for non-renewable or fossil.

q: A renewable energy source is generated from unlimited natural sources and is always _____.
e: A renewable energy source is generated from unlimited natural sources and is always replenished. Consumed or depleted is not this quantity.

q: Solar energy, wind energy, hydro energy, tidal energy, geothermal energy and biomass energy are examples of _____ energy sources.
e: Solar energy, wind energy, hydro energy, tidal energy, geothermal energy and biomass energy are examples of renewable energy sources. Do not trade renewable for non-renewable or fossil.

q: The four major roles of a renewable energy are electricity generation, air and water heating/cooling, the replacement of fossil fuels, and zero or minimal amounts of _____.
e: Heat is energy flowing because of a temperature difference. SI unit is the joule. The four major roles of a renewable energy are electricity generation, air and water heating/cooling, the replacement of fossil fuels, and zero or minimal amounts of greenhouse gases. Do not trade greenhouse gases for oxygen or water vapor.

q: Non-renewable energy comes from sources that will run out or will not be replenished for thousands or even _____ of years.
e: Non-renewable energy comes from sources that will run out or will not be replenished for thousands or even millions of years. Do not trade millions for hundreds or billions.

q: Four main types of non-renewable energy sources are oil, natural gas, coal and _____ energy.
e: Four main types of non-renewable energy sources are oil, natural gas, coal and nuclear energy. Solar or wind is not this quantity.

q: Oil, natural gas and coal are collectively called _____ fuels.
e: Oil, natural gas and coal are collectively called fossil fuels. Do not trade fossil for bio or synthetic.

q: Fossil fuels were formed within the earth from dead plants and animals over _____ of years.
e: Fossil fuels were formed within the earth from dead plants and animals over millions of years. Thousands or decades is not this quantity.

q: Nuclear energy is produced by using elements like uranium and _____.
e: Nuclear energy is produced by using elements like uranium and thorium. Plutonium or radium is not this quantity.

q: Nuclear energy can be used to generate electricity by means of nuclear _____.
e: Nuclear energy can be used to generate electricity by means of nuclear fission. Do not trade fission for fusion or decay.

q: In a nuclear reactor, the nuclear fuel is used to carry out sustained _____ chain reaction to produce electricity.
e: In a nuclear reactor, the nuclear fuel is used to carry out sustained fission chain reaction to produce electricity. Fusion or chemical is not this quantity.

q: Biomass is plant or animal material used as fuel to produce _____ or heat.
e: Cathode rays go in straight lines, bend in electric or magnetic fields, ionize gas, and make fluorescence. Biomass is plant or animal material used as fuel to produce electricity or heat. Do not trade electricity for light or motion.

q: Agricultural waste, wood, charcoal or dried dung are used as _____.
e: Agricultural waste, wood, charcoal or dried dung are used as biomass. Do not trade biomass for fossil fuels or nuclear fuel.

q: Tidal energy is another form of hydro energy that uses tidal currents _____ to drive turbine generator.
e: Tidal energy is another form of hydro energy that uses tidal currents twice-daily to drive turbine generator. Do not trade twice-daily for continuously or monthly.

q: Sun is the _____ source of energy.
e: Sun is the primary source of energy. Do not trade primary for secondary or artificial.

q: With the help of photovoltaic technology, solar energy can be used to generate _____.
e: With the help of photovoltaic technology, solar energy can be used to generate electricity. Biomass or tidal power is not this quantity.
